scheme_name: Chief Minister Sustainable Agriculture Irrigation Scheme - Magel Tyala Shettale (Individual Farm Pond)
description:
The Chief Minister Sustainable Agriculture Irrigation Scheme known as Magel Tyala Shettale was launched by the Government of Maharashtra on 1st April 2018. 

This scheme is designed to promote sustainable agriculture practices through the construction of individual farm ponds. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to enhance irrigation facilities for farmers in Maharashtra. 

The scheme aims to provide irrigation to at least 1.5 million hectares of agricultural land by the year 2025. 

The initiative is particularly focused on small and marginal farmers who often struggle with water scarcity. 

The scheme also seeks to improve the overall agricultural productivity and income levels of farmers. 

Under this scheme, each farmer can receive financial assistance of up to ₹50,000 for the construction of a farm pond. 

The financial assistance is provided in the form of a subsidy, which is 50% of the total cost incurred for the construction of the pond. 

For farmers belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, the subsidy can go up to 75% of the total cost. 

The scheme is applicable to farmers who own land and are engaged in agricultural activities. 

Eligible farmers must have a minimum landholding of 0.5 hectares to qualify for the scheme. 

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There is no upper age limit specified for eligibility. 

Farmers must also be registered under the Maharashtra Land Records system to avail of the benefits. 

To apply for the scheme, farmers must follow a specific process. 

The first step is to visit the nearest Agriculture Department office in their respective district. 

Farmers need to fill out an application form which can be obtained from the office or downloaded from the official website. 

The application form must be accompanied by several documents. 

These documents include proof of land ownership such as a 7/12 extract. 

Farmers must also provide their Aadhaar card for identity verification. 

A bank account statement is required to facilitate the subsidy transfer. 

Additionally, a project report detailing the proposed farm pond's dimensions and expected benefits is necessary. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the Agriculture Department officials. 

The officials will conduct a site visit to verify the details provided in the application. 

If approved, the financial assistance is disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account. 

The timeline for the entire application process can vary but typically takes about 30 to 45 days. 

Disbursement of funds occurs after the completion of the pond construction and submission of necessary completion documents. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Agriculture, Maharashtra. 

Farmers can contact the Agriculture Department at the district level for any queries related to the scheme. 

The contact details for the Agriculture Department can be found on the official Maharashtra government website. 

The scheme has been well-received by farmers, with thousands of applications submitted since its launch. 

As of October 2023, over 1 lakh farm ponds have been constructed under this initiative. 

This has resulted in improved irrigation facilities for more than 2 lakh hectares of agricultural land. 

The scheme has also contributed to a significant increase in crop yields for participating farmers. 

Farmers have reported an increase in their annual income by approximately 30% after the implementation of farm ponds. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of water conservation and sustainable agricultural practices. 

Farm ponds help in rainwater harvesting, which is crucial in drought-prone areas of Maharashtra. 

The initiative aligns with the broader goals of the Government of Maharashtra to promote sustainable development. 

It also supports the national agenda of improving agricultural productivity and farmer welfare. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of initiatives aimed at enhancing the livelihood of farmers in the state. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹500 crores for the implementation of this scheme for the financial year 2023-2024. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted to ensure its effectiveness and reach. 

The government encourages farmers to adopt modern techniques and practices in agriculture through this scheme. 

Educational workshops and training sessions are organized to educate farmers on the benefits of farm ponds. 

The scheme also aims to create awareness about sustainable farming practices among the farming community. 

Overall, the Chief Minister Sustainable Agriculture Irrigation Scheme - Magel Tyala Shettale is a significant step towards improving the agricultural landscape in Maharashtra. 

It addresses the critical issue of water scarcity while promoting sustainable agricultural practices. 

Farmers interested in the scheme are encouraged to act promptly and gather the required documents. 

The scheme represents a vital investment in the future of agriculture in Maharashtra. 

By supporting individual farmers, the government aims to create a ripple effect that benefits the entire agricultural sector. 

The success of this scheme could serve as a model for similar initiatives in other states across India. 

The commitment of the Maharashtra government to farmer welfare is evident through this and other related schemes. 

The scheme not only aims to enhance irrigation but also to empower farmers economically and socially. 

In conclusion, the Chief Minister Sustainable Agriculture Irrigation Scheme - Magel Tyala Shettale is a comprehensive initiative. 

It provides financial assistance and promotes sustainable practices while addressing the pressing issue of water scarcity in agriculture.
